claim: Dim, Eraker & Vilkov (2024), via the Quantpedia summary of the paper: the presence of 0DTEs dampens S&P 500 volatility through a shift in market makers' hedging needs (average effect).
title: Quantpedia summary of Dim-Eraker-Vilkov, 0DTEs and market volatility

claim: Same study: higher net gamma predicts reversal in intraday E-mini order flow and negative high-frequency momentum; dampening effect dissipates after one hour.
quote: a higher net gamma predicts a stronger reversal pattern in the intraday order flow of E-mini futures. The direction is consistent with the observed dampening effect on volatility, and the effect dissipates after one hour.
title: Do S&P500 0DTEs Options Increase Market Volatility? (Quantpedia summary)

claim: Same study: hedging needs on 0DTE days come from pre-existing longer-dated positions that become 0DTE, not intraday 0DTE trading; market makers keep positive net gamma through the expiration day (conditional amplification risk exists via aggregate gamma channel).
quote: market makers maintain a positive portfolio net gamma throughout the 0DTE expiration day.
title: Do S&P500 0DTEs Options Increase Market Volatility? (Quantpedia summary)
